definitionEn: to pass from person to person or place to place, especially information or documents
senseNote: Здесь — «распространяться» (слухи, документы, информация); физическое значение «циркулировать» (кровь, воздух) не рассматриваем.
situation: Information, a document or a rumour moves from one person to another until many people know about it.

examples.text: A rumour started to [[circulate]] that the factory would close by the end of the year.
Please [[circulate]] the meeting notes to everyone who couldn't attend.
Copies of the report [[circulated]] among staff long before it was officially published.

texts: The petition began to [[circulate]] online within hours.
Management asked HR to [[circulate]] the new policy by email.
Stories about the haunted house still [[circulate]] in this town.

badCollocation.noteRu: Болезнь распространяется словом spread, а не circulate: circulate — про слухи, документы и информацию, а не про заразные болезни.

collocationTask.prompt: management asked staff to ___ the safety notice before Friday
collocationTask.explanationRu: Разослать документ коллегам — circulate a notice. Digest значит «переварить, усвоить», witness — «быть свидетелем», postpone — «отложить»: сюда не подходят.

nuance.text: A draft of the proposal was [[circulated]] among senior staff before anyone thought about going public.
nuance.explanationRu: Circulate — неофициально передать по кругу ограниченному кругу людей, часто черновик. Publish — официально выпустить в свет для широкой публики в окончательном виде.

reverse.text: The company finally [[published]] its annual report on its website for anyone to read.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь об официальном публичном выпуске документа, а не о неформальной передаче его по кругу.

fixIt.text: The finance team quietly [[published]] a draft budget among department heads before the board meeting.
fixIt.explanationRu: Черновик, который неофициально передают ограниченному кругу людей, circulate. Publish — официально выпустить в свет для всех.

wordFormation.text: Regular brisk walks are great for keeping the [[circulatory]] system healthy.

rewrite.original: Someone started telling people around the office that the factory might shut down.
rewrite.frame: A rumour started to ____ around the office that the factory might shut down.

definitionEn: the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold or given out
senseNote: Здесь — тираж издания (the paper's circulation); медицинское значение «кровообращение» не рассматриваем.
situation: You talk about how many copies of a newspaper or magazine are printed and sold on a regular basis.

examples.text: The tabloid's daily [[circulation]] has fallen by half since readers moved online.
The magazine boosted its [[circulation]] by offering a free gift with every issue.
Local papers with a small [[circulation]] often struggle to attract big advertisers.

texts: The newspaper's [[circulation]] dropped sharply after the price rise.
Even niche magazines can have a loyal [[circulation]] of dedicated readers.
Advertisers pay more for a spot in a magazine with a huge [[circulation]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Circulation в этом значении — тираж газеты или журнала. Поток покупателей в магазине называют footfall или customer numbers, а не circulation.

collocationTask.prompt: the newspaper's ___ has halved since most readers switched to the app
collocationTask.explanationRu: Тираж газеты — circulation. Furniture (мебель), cutlery (столовые приборы) и footwear (обувь) по смыслу совсем не подходят.

nuance.text: The newspaper's official [[circulation]] is audited every quarter by an independent body.
nuance.explanationRu: Circulation — точное число проданных или выпущенных экземпляров, которое официально проверяют. Readership — более широкое число реальных читателей, часто больше тиража.

reverse.text: Surveys suggest the magazine's true [[readership]] is much larger than its circulation figures suggest.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о реальном числе читателей, а не о числе выпущенных экземпляров.

fixIt.text: The publisher proudly announced that the magazine's [[readership]] had reached two hundred thousand copies sold.
fixIt.explanationRu: Число проданных экземпляров — circulation. Readership — это число читателей, а не «проданные экземпляры».

wordFormation.text: After the free-gift promotion, the tabloid's weekly [[circulation]] jumped by twenty per cent.

rewrite.original: The number of copies of the local paper that get sold every day has been falling for years.
rewrite.frame: The local paper's daily ____ has been falling for years.

definitionEn: the legal status of officially belonging to a particular country
senseNote: Здесь — юридический статус гражданина страны; переносное «сознательность, good citizenship» не рассматриваем.
situation: You talk about the official legal right to belong to a country, often gained by birth, family or a formal application.

examples.text: After living in the country for ten years, she finally applied for [[citizenship]].
Children born here automatically receive [[citizenship]], regardless of their parents' nationality.
He had to give up his original [[citizenship]] in order to become a diplomat.

texts: Many countries now allow dual [[citizenship]].
Passing the exam is the final step toward [[citizenship]].
Her application for [[citizenship]] was approved after two years of waiting.

badCollocation.noteRu: Гражданство не «выигрывают» — его apply for, gain или are granted. Win используют для соревнований и наград.

collocationTask.prompt: after passing the test and the interview, he was finally ___ citizenship
collocationTask.explanationRu: Гражданство официально предоставляют — grant citizenship. Donate (пожертвовать), deliver (доставить) и invite (пригласить) с citizenship не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Ten years after moving here, she was finally granted full [[citizenship]], including the right to vote.
nuance.explanationRu: Citizenship — полное юридическое членство в стране (паспорт, право голоса). Residency — только право проживания, без всех прав гражданина.

reverse.text: His visa gives him temporary [[residency]], but he still can't vote in local elections.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь только право проживания без права голоса — residency, а не полноценное citizenship.

fixIt.text: After passing every test and interview, he was finally granted full [[residency]], including a passport and the right to vote.
fixIt.explanationRu: Право голоса и паспорт даёт citizenship — полноценное гражданство. Residency — только право проживания, без этих прав.

wordFormation.text: After years of living abroad, he decided to apply for [[citizenship]] rather than just a residency permit.

reply.context: A friend messages: "I heard you finally got your passport from your new country! How do you feel?"
options: Amazing, honestly — ten years of paperwork, and now I finally have citizenship.
Amazing — the citizenship lets me stay here for two more years before I renew it.
One is gratified to have finally attained the status of citizenship, following considerable bureaucratic exertion.
reply.explanationRu: Citizenship — постоянный правовой статус, его не «продлевают» как визу. Третий ответ звучит слишком официально для сообщения другу.

definitionEn: relating to a city or town, or to the public duties of its citizens
situation: You describe buildings, events or responsibilities connected with a city or town and the public life of its residents.

examples.text: The mayor unveiled plans for a new [[civic]] centre in the town square.
Voting in local elections is seen by many as a basic [[civic]] duty.
The charity encourages young people to take more [[civic]] pride in their neighbourhood.

texts: The old [[civic]] hall is now used for weddings and concerts.
Volunteering at the shelter is one form of [[civic]] engagement.
Every autumn the town holds a [[civic]] ceremony for local heroes.

badCollocation.noteRu: Civic описывает общественные обязанности и городские учреждения (civic duty, civic pride, civic centre), а не личные события вроде дня рождения.

collocationTask.prompt: many schools now teach ___ responsibility, like voting and volunteering
collocationTask.explanationRu: Про общественные обязанности граждан говорят civic responsibility. Culinary (кулинарный), seasonal (сезонный) и musical (музыкальный) по смыслу не подходят.

nuance.text: Volunteering to clean the local park is a small act of [[civic]] responsibility.
nuance.explanationRu: Civic — конкретно про город и общественные обязанности его жителей (civic duty, civic centre). Civil — более широкое «гражданский» в противовес военному или уголовному (civil rights, civil law).

reverse.text: The new law was a major victory for [[civil]] rights across the country.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о правах человека в целом по всей стране, в противовес государству — civil, а не civic (про городские дела).

fixIt.text: Volunteering to clean the local park is a small act of [[civil]] responsibility.
fixIt.explanationRu: Про обязанности жителей города и местную общественную жизнь говорят civic. Civil — более широкое понятие (civil rights, civil law).

wordFormation.text: American high schools often require a semester of [[civics]] before graduation.

rewrite.original: Every adult has a responsibility to vote and take part in local community life.
rewrite.frame: Every adult has a ____ responsibility to vote and take part in local life.
rewrite.explanationRu: Civic — «гражданский, общественный» (об обязанностях жителя города или страны).

definitionEn: relating to ordinary people and life, rather than the military
situation: You describe people, clothes or aspects of life that are not part of the army, navy or air force.

examples.text: After the ceasefire, [[civilian]] flights were finally allowed to use the airport again.
He left the army last year and is still adjusting to [[civilian]] life.
The report says most of the casualties were [[civilian]], not military personnel.

texts: He swapped his uniform for [[civilian]] clothes before the interview.
The base employs both military staff and [[civilian]] contractors.
International law protects [[civilian]] populations during armed conflict.

badCollocation.noteRu: Civilian описывает то, что не относится к армии; солдат по определению военный (military), сочетание civilian soldier противоречиво.

collocationTask.prompt: after twenty years in the army, he struggled to adjust to ___ life
collocationTask.explanationRu: Жизнь вне армии называют civilian life. Seasonal (сезонный), coastal (прибрежный) и musical (музыкальный) по смыслу не подходят.

nuance.text: The airstrike reportedly killed several [[civilian]] bystanders, not enemy combatants.
nuance.explanationRu: Civilian — гражданский, не военный человек (в противовес combatant). Domestic — «внутренний, отечественный» (в противовес international), про военный статус ничего не говорит.

reverse.text: The airline mainly operates [[domestic]] flights within the country, not international routes.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о рейсах внутри страны в противовес международным — domestic, а не civilian (гражданский, не военный).

fixIt.text: The ceasefire finally allowed [[domestic]] flights to use the airport again, ending months of only military traffic.
fixIt.explanationRu: Противопоставление здесь военным рейсам — нужен civilian (невоенный). Domestic — «внутренний, отечественный», это про другое противопоставление.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Your brother just left the army, right? How's he doing?"
options: He's doing okay, but civilian life still feels strange to him after ten years.
He's doing okay, he just got a really nice civilian promotion at his new job.
He continues to acclimatise to civilian existence following the cessation of his military service.
reply.explanationRu: Civilian описывает невоенную жизнь в целом, а не конкретное повышение на работе. Третий ответ звучит слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: a large group of people, often relatives, who are closely loyal to each other
senseNote: Здесь — обобщённо: сплочённая большая семья или группа по интересам, а не только историческое шотландское значение.
situation: You talk about a large, close family or group of people who are strongly loyal to one another.

examples.text: Every Christmas, the whole [[clan]] gathers at my grandmother's house in the countryside.
The business empire is still controlled by the same wealthy [[clan]] after three generations.
Within the gaming [[clan]], members share tips and compete together in tournaments.

texts: Our whole [[clan]] takes a trip together every summer.
The rival [[clan]] has controlled that market for decades.
She was welcomed into the [[clan]] the moment she married in.

badCollocation.noteRu: Clan подразумевает большую, разветвлённую группу или семью. Про двоих говорят a couple или just the two of them, а не clan.

collocationTask.prompt: every August, the whole ___ gathers at the family farm for a huge reunion
collocationTask.explanationRu: Большую сплочённую семью называют clan. Furniture (мебель), cutlery (столовые приборы) и software (программное обеспечение) по смыслу здесь не подходят.

nuance.text: By the time she turned forty, the whole [[clan]] — aunts, cousins, in-laws — showed up for her birthday.
nuance.explanationRu: Clan — обычно про родственную, тесно связанную группу (расширенная семья). Tribe — более широкое сообщество с общим языком и традициями, часто историческое или этническое.

reverse.text: Anthropologists studied how the [[tribe]] passed down its traditions and language across many generations.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о крупной этнической общности с общим языком и традициями — tribe, а не clan (родственная группа).

fixIt.text: Every Christmas, aunts, uncles and cousins from the whole [[tribe]] squeeze into my grandmother's tiny kitchen.
fixIt.explanationRu: Про большую сплочённую семью говорят clan. Tribe — более крупная историческая или этническая общность, а не просто родня.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Are you doing anything for your grandmother's ninetieth birthday?"
options: Yes, the whole clan is flying in from three different countries for it.
Yes, I'm inviting my whole clan — just me and my roommate, actually.
Indeed, the entirety of our familial clan shall be convening for the celebratory occasion.
reply.explanationRu: Clan — большая, а не маленькая группа из двух человек. Третий ответ звучит слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: the quality of being clear and easy to understand
situation: You praise or ask for an explanation, plan or piece of writing that is easy to follow and free of confusion.

examples.text: The lawyer explained the contract with impressive [[clarity]], and no one had any questions left.
After months of confusion, she finally felt some [[clarity]] about what she wanted from her career.
The report lacks [[clarity]]; half the team misunderstood the main recommendation.

texts: The teacher explained the rule with real [[clarity]].
I need more [[clarity]] before I can sign the contract.
Her essay is a model of [[clarity]] and structure.

badCollocation.noteRu: Clarity — существительное («ясность»), а не прилагательное. Про человека, который ясно мыслит, говорят a clear thinker или she thinks with clarity.

collocationTask.prompt: could you explain the new pricing policy with more ___?
collocationTask.explanationRu: Просьба объяснить яснее — with more clarity. Luggage (багаж), traffic (трафик) и furniture (мебель) по смыслу с explain не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Her lawyer explained the options with such [[clarity]] that the whole family finally understood their choices.
nuance.explanationRu: Clarity — ясность объяснения, лёгкость понимания. Certainty — уверенность в том, что что-то истинно или произойдёт; это про факты, а не про то, как их излагают.

reverse.text: Doctors still can't say with any [[certainty]] whether the treatment will work.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь об уверенности в фактах, а не о ясности объяснения — certainty, а не clarity.

fixIt.text: The new manager explained the reorganisation plan with impressive [[certainty]], and everyone left understanding exactly what would happen next.
fixIt.explanationRu: Здесь важно, что объяснение было понятным — clarity, а не то, что менеджер был уверен в фактах (certainty).

wordFormation.text: She always explains grammar rules with such [[clarity]] that nobody feels lost.

reply.context: A friend says: "I read the new tax rules three times and I'm still confused."
options: Yeah, they could really use more clarity — even accountants find them confusing.
Totally, the printing is so blurry, they definitely need more clarity on that leaflet.
Indeed, greater clarity in the drafting of said regulations would be most welcome.
reply.explanationRu: Clarity здесь — про понятность объяснения, а не про чёткость печати. Третий ответ звучит слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: a serious disagreement or a short, sharp conflict between people, groups or ideas
senseNote: Здесь — конфликт или столкновение (мнений, интересов, групп людей); значение «не сочетаться» (о цветах, расписании) не рассматриваем.
situation: You describe a serious disagreement, a fight, or a sudden conflict of interests between two people, groups or ideas.

examples.text: Police were called to break up a [[clash]] between rival fans outside the stadium.
The meeting ended in a bitter [[clash]] over the company's new direction.
There's a real [[clash]] of personalities between the two lead actors.

texts: A border [[clash]] left several soldiers injured on both sides.
Their [[clash]] over the will divided the whole family.
The debate turned into a heated [[clash]] between the two candidates.

badCollocation.noteRu: Clash в этом значении — конфликт между людьми, группами или мнениями (a clash of opinions), а не про предметы мебели.

collocationTask.prompt: the two department heads have had a personality ___ ever since the merger
collocationTask.explanationRu: О несовместимости характеров говорят a personality clash. Harmony (гармония), blend (смешение) и balance (баланс) означают обратное — согласие.

nuance.text: Tensions finally boiled over into a violent [[clash]] outside the courthouse on Friday afternoon.
nuance.explanationRu: Clash — короткое, резкое столкновение или стычка, часто один конкретный эпизод. Conflict — более широкое и длительное состояние противостояния.

reverse.text: The two nations have been locked in [[conflict]] over the border for nearly a decade.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о долгом, затяжном противостоянии, а не об одном резком эпизоде — conflict, а не clash.

fixIt.text: Tensions between the rival fans finally boiled over into a violent [[conflict]] outside the stadium on Saturday night.
fixIt.explanationRu: Один резкий эпизод столкновения — clash. Conflict — более длительное, растянутое противостояние, а не одна вспышка за вечер.

rewrite.original: The two candidates strongly disagreed with each other during last night's television debate.
rewrite.frame: The two candidates had a heated ____ during last night's television debate.
rewrite.explanationRu: Clash — резкое столкновение мнений или сторон.

definitionEn: a system for dividing things into groups according to shared features
situation: You describe a system that sorts animals, films, jobs or other things into named groups or categories.

examples.text: Under the new film [[classification]], the movie was rated suitable only for adults.
Scientists are still debating the correct [[classification]] of several newly discovered insects.
The job's official [[classification]] determines which benefits an employee receives.

texts: The library uses its own [[classification]] system for rare manuscripts.
The disease's exact [[classification]] changed after new research came out.
Under this [[classification]], tomatoes technically count as a fruit.

badCollocation.noteRu: Classification — формальная система категорий (для животных, фильмов, профессий), а не неформальная характеристика человека вроде «друг».

collocationTask.prompt: under the official ___, this film is not suitable for children under fifteen
collocationTask.explanationRu: Официальную систему возрастных категорий фильма называют classification. Soundtrack (саундтрек), screenplay (сценарий) и premiere (премьера) по смыслу не подходят.

nuance.text: The board is reviewing the film's [[classification]] after complaints from parents.
nuance.explanationRu: Classification — вся система деления на группы или процесс отнесения к группе. Category — сама одна группа внутри такой системы.

reverse.text: This film falls into the strictest age [[category]] the board has.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь об одной конкретной группе внутри системы — category, а не обо всей системе classification.

fixIt.text: The board is reviewing the film's age [[category]] system after complaints from parents about violent scenes.
fixIt.explanationRu: Всю систему деления на возрастные группы называют classification. Category — только одна отдельная группа внутри неё.

wordFormation.text: Officials are struggling to agree on the correct [[classification]] of the new disease.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Is this new horror film okay for my ten-year-old to watch?"
options: Actually no — its classification says it's for over-fifteens only, so I'd wait a few years.
Actually no — its classification is way too scary for me personally, I couldn't sleep.
One should consult the applicable classification prior to permitting a minor's viewing thereof.
reply.explanationRu: Classification — официальная система возрастных ограничений, а не личное впечатление от фильма. Третий ответ звучит как юридический документ.
